page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine shape built on Intel Xeon 8358 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated virtual CPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM allocated per virtual core. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the instance.

The virtual server configuration does not bundle local storage disks, requiring external network-attached block volumes for persistent data retention and operating system hosting. Additionally, VM.Standard3.Flex.8-64 provides no discrete GPU acceleration units, directing all computational operations to the dedicated CPU cores. An architectural tradeoff involves relying on network interfaces for storage traffic while gaining the performance consistency of dedicated physical execution threads rather than shared or burstable CPU resources.

From a resource allocation perspective, pairing 64.0 GB of RAM with 16 dedicated vCPUs offers a predictable balance for general enterprise workloads without unnecessary cost overhead from excess memory capacity or unused GPU hardware. VM.Standard3.Flex.8-64 is well suited for mid-sized relational databases, application servers, enterprise web serving layers, continuous integration workers, and containerized microservice deployments.
